hints: Look closely at the repeating unit in brackets. Count how many different sugar rings you see and notice that one is upside-down compared to the other.
Trace the central O bridge. Check which carbon positions it connects on the left ring and the right ring, carbon 1 is next to the ring O, then count around.
walkthrough:
**Look at what is repeating**

Look inside the large brackets with the small n. You can see two six-sided sugar rings joined together.

Notice the COOH group is on top in the left ring but on the bottom in the right ring. That flip tells you these are two slightly different monomers, and they alternate in opposite directions.

**Identify the glycosidic bond**

The two rings are linked by a single O atom in the middle. This is a glycosidic bond formed by condensation.

If you number each hexose ring starting at the ring O as position 5 to 1, you will find the bridge connects carbon 1 of one sugar to carbon 4 of the next. So it is a 1,4 glycosidic bond.

**Put it together to choose**

So alginic acid is a linear polymer made from two types of uronic acid monomers joined by 1,4 links, very much like cellulose.

That matches only option B.

options.A: It is linear, but the bridge is between carbons 1 and 4, not 1 and 6. 1,6 bonds are for branching, which you do not see here.
options.B: Correct. The repeat unit shows two different hexose acid monomers linked by 1,4 glycosidic bonds to form a linear chain.
options.C: The first part is true, alternate sugars are flipped, but this is seen in cellulose, not glycogen. Glycogen monomers all face the same way with 1,4 and 1,6 branches.
options.D: Condensation joins hexose sugars together and releases water, water is removed not joined in. This reverses what happens in condensation.
